The per-bookmark actions work. Open the two layouts below — they're identical except how a bookmark's actions are arranged. In **each**, try these three things:

1. **Open the original page** — click a bookmark's **title** (or its image). It opens the real page in a new browser tab.
2. **Edit its address** — press **Edit**; you'll see a new **"Address (link)"** field alongside title and description. Change it and Save — the bookmark now points to the new address.
3. **Delete it** — a confirmation appears (*"Delete permanently? This can't be undone."*); Cancel keeps it, Delete removes it for good.

The layouts differ in how actions are presented:

- **Option A — everything as buttons:** http://maker:4001/action-a.html
  *Edit*, the read-status toggle, and *Delete* are all visible on each card.

- **Option B — Edit shown, the rest under "More":** http://maker:4001/action-b.html
  *Edit* stays on the card; the status change and *Delete* live under a **More ▾** menu.

Why the layout matters: you've also asked for **Archive** and **bulk actions** next, so the number of per-bookmark actions is going to grow — Option B keeps cards tidy as that happens, Option A keeps everything one click away.

A couple of assumptions to check: opening always uses a **new tab**; **Delete is permanent and always asks first**; and editing the address **doesn't silently re-fetch** the page details (you stay in control of them).

**Which action layout do you prefer — and do opening, editing the address, and deleting all behave as you'd want?**
